results.title: Pace Digitek Secures ₹488 Crore NTPC GE BESS Order, Strengthens Storage Business
results.description: Pace Digitek secured a ₹488.46 crore BESS order from NTPC GE Power Services as it scales battery storage manufacturing capacity to 10 GWh by FY27.

results.title: Biketaxi riders seek clear registration process relief on challans
results.description: DW Bureau nbspChandigarh Sep 21 A delegation of the Tricity Bike Riders Union met senior BJP leader and BJP National Council member Sanjay Tandon on Monday and raised issues related to biketaxi operations registration and challans in ChandigarhLed by Union president Sahil the delegation sought a clear mechanism for registration and a transparent framework for operating bike taxis The riders said enforcement action and challans were affecting their livelihoods and urged authorities to provide a lawful mechanism to continue their workTandon said the concerns of the riders should be addressed through dialogue and a practical approach He assured the delegation that he would take up the issues with the concerned departmentsThere is a need for clear guidelines and a transparent system so that riders understand their rights and responsibilities and can work in accordance with the rules Tandon saidThe delegation claimed that enforcement action had intensified after the suspension of licences of major private appbased aggregators in Chandigarh It cited reports of 231 vehicles being challaned and 16 impounded between September 9 and 12The riders also discussed the recently launched Bharat Taxi service in Chandigarh which includes bike services and follows a cooperative model They said they were willing to comply with applicable rules and sought a sustainable avenue for employmentChandigarh BJP leaders Ravinder Thakur and Pradeep Yadav who accompanied the delegation also assured the riders that their concerns would be raised with the administration

results.title: Ladakh’s village heads get over 233% hike in monthly emoluments
results.description: Ladakh’s village heads, locally known as ‘Gobas’, are in for a major financial boost; their monthly emoluments being increased more than three-fold from Rs 1,500 to Rs 5,000 after Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena approved the long-pending revision on Monday.
